source.title: Bridging Lottery Ticket and Grokking: Understanding Grokking from Inner Structure of Networks
source.authors: Gouki Minegishi; Yusuke Iwasawa; Yutaka Matsuo

record.tranche_reason: The study measures delayed generalization and how pruning, structural changes, and norm controls affect it. These are conceptual tests of the grokking claims, not a direct reproduction of the original training recipe.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own training and test accuracy results, structural measurements, and controlled experiments. It also cites grokking results from other work; those cited results are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The dense base models reproduce delayed generalization on modular arithmetic (Transformer and MLP), sparse parity and MNIST. The paper then tests weight-norm and weight-decay explanations with matched-norm controls and with weight decay applied from memorized solutions. It also tracks structural progress measures against test accuracy. Its main lever, lottery tickets taken from an already generalized network, uses the trained solution and does not show delay arising otherwise. Those rows are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that grokked tickets sharply reduce delayed generalization. They argue good subnetwork structure, not weight norm or sparsity alone, explains this, and that structural change coincides with the test-accuracy rise. They add that weight decay works as a structure explorer, unnecessary once good structure is found. They also claim edge-popup pruning alone can turn a memorizing network into a generalizing one.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses lottery-ticket pruning, norm- and sparsity-matched controls, structural measurements, and edge-popup mask optimization rather than reproducing the original grokking intervention. It mainly studies modular arithmetic, with additional regression, parity, and MNIST tasks.
record.method_sensitivity: Pruning rate and pruning time affect the reported generalization speed; the paper reports that a pruning rate of 0.7 minimizes τgrok, that a rate of 0.9 can fail to generalize, and that tickets acquired before 25k epochs do not fully generalize. It also reports differences across pruning methods.

fits_no_version.finding: Lottery tickets pruned from an already-generalized network (grokked tickets) nearly eliminate the delay across tasks and architectures. The mask also shows periodic Fourier structure early in training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Masks taken from the generalized solution remove grokking delay; the delay reflects a search for subnetwork structure.

fits_no_version.finding: Pruning-at-initialization at the ticket's sparsity does not reduce the delay and often hurts generalization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparsity alone does not explain grokking acceleration.

fits_no_version.finding: Edge-popup mask optimization without weight updates moves a memorizing network to 0.92 test accuracy. Combined with weight decay, it generalizes faster than weight decay alone.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Structural search alone can convert memorization into generalization.

record.problems: Several accuracy and structural results are available only in figures without numeric values in the text. The paper reports experiments with three seeds for some results but does not give uncertainty for most plotted curves. It does not vary training-set size, so it cannot address the claimed dependence of delay on set size.
record.rows_left_out: No additional result rows left out.

untested.parts: Dependence of the delay on training-set size; the split is fixed at 40%.
Removal of memorizing components; whether the measures anticipate rather than coincide with the jump; Nanda-style Fourier circuit progress measures.
Text and molecules; switching grokking on or off via initialization scale or weight norm; the lazy-to-rich transition.
Critical dataset size, ungrokking, and circuit efficiency.
All of it. AdamW is used throughout with no optimizer or precision controls.

missing.what: τgrok (tgen/tmem) by pruning rate, including the dense model at rate 0. This would quantify the base-model delay; the mapping of values to rates is garbled in the text.

Graph metrics over training (weighted spectral gap, Ramanujan gap, average path length, clustering) against test accuracy. The Ramanujan gap decreases steadily from the start, a possible continuous progress measure.
Base-model L2 norm falls as test accuracy rises toward a 'generalized zone'.
Grokked ticket at the critical pruning rate 0.81 reaches full generalization with zero weight decay.
Jaccard distance coinciding with test-accuracy change on polynomial regression and sparse parity.

record.verdict_notes: Most evidence is figure-only. The base-model delay is never stated numerically. Rows r25–r28 and r21–r24 compare the study's own method against weight decay. For r23 the record notes the text's 0.92 against the table's 0.84 at epoch 1400; 0.92 is the epoch-2000 value. Tranche T2: the base reproduction follows the original recipe (AdamW, weight decay 1.0, p=67), but the paper's tests are of alternative explanations.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not vary training-set size or test whether smaller training sets require more optimization.

It measures structural change and periodicity, but does not establish that memorizing components are removed later or that the measured changes anticipate, rather than coincide with, the test-accuracy rise.
It reports results on MNIST and other tasks, but does not test initialization-scale or weight-norm switches, or a lazy-to-rich transition.
LLM pretraining and fine-tuning on realistic data.
It does not test a critical dataset size or ungrokking below such a size, nor directly measure circuit efficiency.
Whether runs converge to the same identifiable algorithm across architectures and hyperparameters.
Adaptive-optimizer instabilities and floating-point limits in the softmax.
